hints: Find the normal reaction $R = 3g \cos 30^\circ = 15\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$ and calculate friction force: $F = \mu R = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{12}(15\sqrt{3}) = 3.75\text{ N}$.
Set up the work-energy equation for the upward motion from A to B: $\frac{1}{2}m u^2 = mg d \sin 30^\circ + F d$, and solve for the distance $d = 5.12\text{ m}$.
Set up the work-energy equation for the downward motion from B back to A: $\frac{1}{2}m v^2 = mg d \sin 30^\circ - F d$, and evaluate the return speed $v$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the normal reaction and friction force on the inclined plane:
$$R = 3g \cos 30^\circ = 3(10)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 15\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$
$$F = \mu R = \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{12}\right)(15\sqrt{3}) = \frac{45}{12} = 3.75\text{ N}$$

Apply the work-energy principle for motion from A to instantaneous rest at B over distance $d$:
$$\frac{1}{2}m u^2 = mg d \sin 30^\circ + F d$$
$$\frac{1}{2}(3)(8^2) = 3(10) d (0.5) + 3.75 d \implies 96 = 15d + 3.75d = 18.75d$$
$$d = \frac{96}{18.75} = 5.12\text{ m}$$

Calculate the work done against friction in each direction:
$$W_F = F d = 3.75 \times 5.12 = 19.2\text{ J}$$

Apply the work-energy principle for the return journey from B down to A:
$$\frac{1}{2}m v^2 = mg d \sin 30^\circ - W_F$$
$$\frac{1}{2}(3)v^2 = 3(10)(5.12)(0.5) - 19.2 = 76.8 - 19.2 = 57.6\text{ J}$$
$$1.5 v^2 = 57.6 \implies v^2 = \frac{57.6}{1.5} = 38.4$$
$$v = \sqrt{38.4} \approx 6.20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the normal reaction force and frictional force.
Particle P of mass $m = 3\text{ kg}$ is on a rough slope inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal.
Normal reaction:
$$R = mg \cos 30^\circ = 3 \times 10 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 15\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$
Given $\mu = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{12}$, the magnitude of friction while moving is:
$$F = \mu R = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{12} \times 15\sqrt{3} = \frac{15 \times 3}{12} = \frac{45}{12} = 3.75\text{ N}$$

Step 2: Upward journey from A to B (distance $d$).
Initial kinetic energy at A:
$$KE_A = \frac{1}{2}m u^2 = \frac{1}{2}(3)(8^2) = 1.5 \times 64 = 96\text{ J}$$
At point B, the particle is instantaneously at rest ($KE_B = 0$).
Gain in gravitational potential energy:
$$\Delta PE = mg h = mg(d \sin 30^\circ) = 3 \times 10 \times 0.5 \times d = 15d$$
Work done against friction:
$$W_{\text{friction}} = F \times d = 3.75d$$
By the work-energy principle:
$$KE_A = \Delta PE + W_{\text{friction}}$$
$$96 = 15d + 3.75d = 18.75d$$
$$d = \frac{96}{18.75} = \frac{96}{\frac{75}{4}} = \frac{384}{75} = 5.12\text{ m}$$
The work done against friction is:
$$W_{\text{friction}} = 3.75 \times 5.12 = 19.2\text{ J}$$

Step 3: Downward journey from B to A.
The particle starts from rest at B and accelerates down the slope to A.
Loss in gravitational potential energy:
$$\Delta PE_{\text{lost}} = 15d = 15 \times 5.12 = 76.8\text{ J}$$
Friction opposes motion down the slope, doing work $W_{\text{friction}} = 19.2\text{ J}$.
By the work-energy principle:
$$KE_A = \Delta PE_{\text{lost}} - W_{\text{friction}}$$
$$\frac{1}{2}(3)v^2 = 76.8 - 19.2 = 57.6\text{ J}$$
$$1.5v^2 = 57.6$$
$$v^2 = \frac{57.6}{1.5} = 38.4$$
$$v = \sqrt{38.4} \approx 6.19677\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 6.20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
